name: What's yum?
description:
I think,
y stands for Yellowdog
u stands for Update
m stands for Manager

Quick man-page check confirms I was wrong, Its Yellowdog Updater Modified. It improves the installation RPMs. yum will search for different repos (think of repo as different sites all around the world) and install an RPM along with its dependent RPMs.
Thus solves the problem of system administrators to resolve dependency for each package! (Which we call "dependency hell". Honestly Its _the_ real hell.)

name: Finding correct package
description:
yum comes with lot of options. Lets assume we want to install C-Compiler. You know, C-Compiler must of part of some package,right? Lets search for it.
yum search

yum search cc
gcc stands for GNU C-Compiler. If you know the binary you can also use
yum whatprovides cc
Every user use 'ls' command. Assume 'ls' is missing or deleted by mistake. Now, Do you know which package provides 'ls'?

name: Installing package
description:
Once you know package name, installing it is as easy as :
yum install gcc
Above command will install the required package along with all its dependency. As you noticed it asks for 'Y/N', If you want install packages without being prompted , just add -y to yum.
yum -y install gcc.

name: updating package
description:
Assume tomorrow, new version of gcc got released and its available on your repo. To update to latest version, all you need to do is:
yum update gcc

name: removing a package
description:
For some reason, you want to uninstall C-compiler (may be to prevent hacking via c-code). Just do remove,
yum remove gcc
Note : This might remove some other packages which are dependenton gcc.

name: updating all packages
description:
You want to ensure that the system up-to-date. I mean it contains latest version of all packages. Here is the way to do it: One we aleady mentioned using 'update' with packagename, like
yum update pkg1

yum update pkg2
etc. Now the simple question, how to find all installed packages so that we can update. Don't worry yum provides something called ... (read on)

name: List all installed packages
description:
Something called
yum list installed
which will display all installed packages. All you need to do is to run update on these packages! nice right? :) What? Do you serious think its nice? Checking my localdesktop it has around 2743 pacakges. Are you going to run update 2743 times? No way! What the right way to ensure system is up-to-date. Just do :
yum update
that's all yum will takecare of the rest :). Now thats really cool :D

name: Download the packages
description:
Lets just say, you want to download the package first, then install it later! because you find network speed is good now, so just want to download them first then install later.

For such cases, there isutility named yumdownloader. Its usage is :

yumdownloader nginx
This will download the package on your current directory but won't install.

name: installing rpm via yum
description:
Okay, in previous step we downloaded nginx (webserver). We know it might have lot of dependent pacakge. To tell yum, we want yum to resolve that problem by itself and install it. We can do
yum localinstall file.rpm

yum localinstall nginx-1.2.9-1.fc18.x86_64.rpm
So here we learned how to install any rpm file using yum localinstall option. This is really a nice option to have!

name: Finding more details about package
description:
In order to find informations like version,size,license and url of a package we can do
yum info gcc

name: Reinstall and downgrade a package
description:
This command will uninstall existing package and re-install it again. Its different from update - This will install the package with exact same version.
yum reinstall nginx
This 'downgrade' command does exact opposite of yum update package. I'll let you to decide what it might do. You should be able to figure it out from command like :
yum downgrade nginx
